summary: Insert Object Into Array: appends an existing object, referenced by its id, to a shared array when Do fires.
description: When `add` (Do) fires, resolves `collectionId` (Array Id) to the shared array and `modifyId` (Object Id) to the shared object, appends the object to the end of the array, and reports one outcome: `done` (Done) when the object was added, or `unchanged` (Unchanged) when the array already held it — arrays hold each object once, so a repeat insert changes nothing. `failure` (Failure) fires when either id is unset. `completed` (Completed) fires after all three. Because arrays are shared by id, every Array node and Repeater bound to the same Array Id sees the new item immediately.
whenToUse: Adding items to a local shared array — typically right after Create New Object has created the object to add. For removing use Remove Object From Array; for cloud data use the record nodes instead (nothing here is persisted).

ports.add: Signal input (Do); performs the insert after other inputs have settled.
ports.collectionId: Value input: id of the shared array to append to.
ports.modifyId: Connection-only value input: the id of the object to insert — typically Create New Object's `id` output.
ports.done: Signal (Done); fires after the object has been appended.
ports.unchanged: Signal (Unchanged); fires when the object was already in the array, so nothing was added. Not a failure — the array holds what the author asked for.
ports.failure: Signal (Failure); fires when the array or the object could not be resolved. `error` carries the reason.
ports.completed: Signal (Completed); fires after every Do whatever the outcome. Wire this to carry on regardless of whether anything changed.

patterns: Create New Object `created` → `add` and `id` → `modifyId`: the canonical create-then-insert flow.
antiPatterns: Trying to insert a raw value or JS object — `modifyId` takes an object id, not the data itself; create an object first with Create New Object.
